subject: Set outputOptions for all outputs of a module from parent application

messages.author: b77c540835bb3b48
messages.subject: Set outputOptions for all outputs of a module from parent application
parts:
Hi,

I would like to set the outputOptions of all the outputs of a module that I call in a parent application. In particular, I would like to toggle the suspendWhenHidden flag for all outputs. The motivation is that I would like to pre-calculate certain things before the user continues to the next step (which is hidden and thus Shiny suspends the outputs by default).

My problem is that by design the outputs of the module are not directly accessible from the parent application. However controlling the suspendWhenHidden option would still be important for the parent application and thus the decision whether to suspend could be left with the parent application I think.

The following "hack" seems to work, however I was wondering if anyone is aware of a more elegant and potentially more robust solution.

suspendModuleWhenHidden <- function(output,session,id,suspendWhenHidden=TRUE) {
  ns <- session$ns
  output_names <- session$clientData %>%
    reactiveValuesToList() %>%
    names %>%
    {.[grepl(NS(ns(id))(""),.,fixed=TRUE)]} %>%
    {gsub("^output[_]","",.,fixed=FALSE)} %>%
    {gsub("[_]hidden$","",.,fixed=FALSE)} %>%
    {gsub(NS(ns(id))(""),"",.,fixed=TRUE)}

  for (output_id in output_names) {
    try({outputOptions(output,gsub(ns(""),"",NS(ns(id))(output_id),fixed=TRUE),suspendWhenHidden=suspendWhenHidden)},silent = TRUE)
  }
  return(0)
}

Any assistance is very much appreciated.

Thank you,

Andras

messages.author: d6ebe55625e8e5a2
messages.subject: Re: Set outputOptions for all outputs of a module from parent application
parts:
It would be nice to be able to set stuff like this from the parent application. I'm adding this question to an existing Shiny Github issue along similar lines (https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/1546). Maybe we'll have a better answer in the future! For now, here's another way. Basically, you can pass a reactive from the parent to the module as an argument, specifying the wanted value for suspendWhenHidden. On the module, you set an observer for this reactive, and alter the outputOptions accordingly.

library(shiny)

modUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  tagList(
    plotOutput(ns("p1")),
    plotOutput(ns("p2"))
  )
}
mod <- function(input, output, session, numPoints, suspendWhenHidden) {
  observe({
    if (!suspendWhenHidden()) {  # when susppendWhenHidden = FALSE
      outputOptions(output, "p1", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
      outputOptions(output, "p2", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
    } else { # when susppendWhenHidden = TRUE
      outputOptions(output, "p1", suspendWhenHidden = TRUE)
      outputOptions(output, "p2", suspendWhenHidden = TRUE)
    }
  })
  
  output$p1 <- renderPlot({
    Sys.sleep(1)
    plot(runif(numPoints()))
  })
  
  output$p2 <- renderPlot({
    Sys.sleep(1)
    plot(runif(numPoints()))
  })
}

ui <- fixedPage(
  checkboxInput("suspendWhenHidden", "suspendWhenHidden", value = TRUE),
  tabsetPanel(
    tabPanel("Module", modUI("modID")),
    tabPanel("Other stuff", numericInput("points", "How many point to plot", 10))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  callModule(mod, "modID", reactive(input$points), reactive(input$suspendWhenHidden))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Hi Barbara,

Thanks very much for your reply! That is indeed a solution for the case when you are in control of the module development as well. In our current workflow however, some people (potentially relatively new to Shiny) are contributing by creating analysis modules, whilst others are purely writing wrappers around them for a larger application.

I will be following the github issue then, thanks for the pointer!

Best,

Andras

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Set outputOptions for all outputs of a module from parent application
parts:
I just realized this can be worked around today by using an observer to inspect names(session$clientData):

unsuspendAll <- function(session = getDefaultReactiveDomain()) {
  observe({
    pattern <- "^output_(.*?)_hidden$"
    
    ids <- names(session$clientData) %>%
      grep(pattern, ., value = TRUE) %>%
      sub(pattern, "\\1", .)
    for (id in ids) {
      print(id)
      outputOptions(session$output, id, suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
    }
  })
}

Define this function in global.R or at the top of server.R or app.R, and call it from inside of your app's server function. As written, it will apply to *all* outputs of your app--past, present, and future. You can tweak/extend it if you'd like to limit it to particular modules or whatever.

Note that I originally tried testing this on plotOutput/renderPlot. plotOutput presents a second challenge: even if suspendWhenHidden=FALSE, by default, renderPlot will try to set the plot output size to the same width/height of the plotOutput, which will be 0 by 0 pixels when it's not actually visible. You can work around this if necessary by providing explicit width and height arguments to the renderPlot() function call itself (NOT the call to plotOutput and not any function calls inside the renderPlot code block). For example, renderPlot({...}, width=400, height=300).
